title: Securities Dealing Policy

tiers.name: Elders People
tiers.description: Each Elders Group director, officer and employee, and each contractor and consultant whose terms of engagement apply the Policy to them. Subject to the insider trading law, Blackout Periods, the 6-month short-term/short-selling ban, and the absolute ban on Derivatives over remuneration securities; not subject to any formal pre-clearance procedure.

tiers.name: Designated Persons
tiers.description: Each director, each Company Secretary, each member of the Elders Executive Committee, all key management personnel named in the annual financial statements, and any other Elders Person with material or regular access to price-sensitive information. Additionally subject to Section 4.2 prior written notification and approval before dealing, and the Section 4.5 margin lending prohibition.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Directors of Elders, a subset of Designated Persons who must separately confirm dealings to the Company Secretary within 2 days for market disclosure purposes.

tiers.name: Related Persons
tiers.description: Family members who may influence or be influenced by an Elders Person, business partners, entities of which the person is a director or chief executive, trusts where the person is a beneficiary, and entities the person can control. Designated Persons must take steps to ensure Related Persons observe the notification/approval procedure and do not deal outside Open Periods or engage in short-term dealing.

definitions.hedging_definition: any other transaction in financial products that operates to limit the economic risk associated with holding the relevant securities

windows.end_anchor: close of trading on ASX on the day after the Company announces its half year financial result to ASX in that same year
close of trading on ASX on the day after the Company announces its full year financial result to ASX in that same year

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: Elders may notify an Elders Person in writing that a specified Security is 'blacklisted' for a stated period; the person must not deal in it during that time unless they first follow the Section 4.2 notification and approval procedure as if they were a Designated Person. The person must not discuss the fact of the blacklisting with anyone other than the Chairman, another director, the CEO or the Company Secretary and General Counsel, so the existence of the blacklist is confidential to that extent.

rules.detail: Absolute ban applying to every Elders Person regardless of Designated Person status, but textually confined to Securities 'issued as part of your remuneration' (e.g. LTI, DESP or EESP shares, options, performance or service rights); covers both unvested and vested remuneration securities. Collars are expressly listed as an example of a Derivative in the definitions section.
rules.evidence: Therefore, you must not use, nor allow to be used, any Derivatives in relation to any Elders Securities issued as part of your remuneration whether vested or unvested.

rules.detail: For Elders Securities not issued as remuneration, entering a derivative is only a 'deal': it must occur in an Open Period and without Inside Information, but no formal clearance is required for non-Designated Persons.

carve_outs: vesting of performance rights or exercise of options under an employee incentive scheme, and the subsequent sale of the underlying Elders shares within a 6 month period

short_term.evidence: you must not deal in the same Elders securities within any 6-month period or engage in short selling of Elders Securities. This prohibition does not restrict the vesting of performance rights or exercise of options under an employee incentive scheme, and the subsequent sale of the underlying Elders shares within a 6 month period. Similarly, the sale of Elders shares at the end of a restriction period applying under such a scheme is not prohibited.

a trust of which a Designated Person acts as trustee may deal in Securities if: the Designated Person, or a Related Party of the Designated Person, is not a beneficiary of the trust; the decision to deal in the relevant Securities is taken without reference to, and independently of, the Designated Person; and the Designated Person is not the sole trustee.

exemption_authority: The Company Secretary and General Counsel (or the Chairman, where that person is the applicant) may in their sole discretion grant clearance to dispose of (not acquire) securities during a Blackout Period for severe financial difficulty or other exceptional circumstances such as a Family Court order. There is no exemption from the absolute Section 3.6 derivatives ban on remuneration securities, and no board-level waiver mechanism is described.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Derivatives includes: derivatives within the meaning given in section 761D of the Corporations Act (such as options, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants, caps and collars); and any other transaction in financial products that operates to limit the economic risk associated with holding the relevant securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The policy expressly identifies a 'collar' as a Derivative, so a bank-provided equity collar over Elders securities issued as remuneration is unambiguously and absolutely banned under Section 3.6, irrespective of vesting state or Designated Person status.

bespoke_clauses.topic: derivatives ban limited to remuneration securities
bespoke_clauses.clause: you must not use, nor allow to be used, any Derivatives in relation to any Elders Securities issued as part of your remuneration whether vested or unvested.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The absolute derivatives ban is textually confined to securities 'issued as part of your remuneration'; a collar over Elders shares an executive acquired other than as remuneration (e.g. purchased on-market) is not caught by this ban and is instead only an ordinary 'deal' subject to Open Period timing and, for Designated Persons, the Section 4.2 clearance procedure.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons must not acquire Elders Securities subject to a margin lending arrangement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This bans only acquiring shares using margin finance; pledging already-held vested shares as collateral for a bank loan is not literally an 'acquisition subject to margin lending' and instead falls within the general 'use of Securities as security' limb of the dealing definition, which is only permitted_with_clearance, not banned outright — a critical distinction for structuring the collar's loan leg.

bespoke_clauses.clause: deal includes ... the use of the Securities as security or the grant of any encumbrance over the Securities
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Pledging vested shares to the bank as security for the loan is expressly a 'deal', so it must occur inside an Open Period, outside possession of Inside Information, and (for a Designated Person) after Section 4.2 written approval — but it is not prohibited.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons must take steps to ensure that their Related Persons understand and act in accordance with the terms of this Policy ... A Designated Person might sometimes act as trustee of a trust ... a trust of which a Designated Person acts as trustee may deal in Securities if the decision to deal ... is taken without reference to, and independently of, the Designated Person.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Routing the collar or a pledge through a spouse, controlled company or family trust does not avoid the restrictions unless the narrow independent-trustee criteria are met; otherwise the Designated Person remains responsible for the Related Person's compliance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a director of Elders must notify the Company Secretary of Elders ... as soon as practicable after any dealing in Elders Securities occurs and, in any case, no more than two days afterwards.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Entry into, or unwind of, a collar or its financing by a director will be reported internally within 2 days and is likely to feed into ASX disclosure of director's interest changes.

summary: A funded collar over Elders securities that were issued to the executive as remuneration (typical LTI, DESP or EESP shares) is flatly prohibited: Section 3.6 bans any Derivative — expressly including 'collars' — over such securities whether vested or unvested, for every Elders Person, with no clearance route or exemption. Where the underlying vested shares were instead acquired other than as remuneration (e.g. on-market purchases), the collar is merely a 'deal': it must be entered in an Open Period (outside the 1 March-to-results and 1 September-to-results Blackout Periods) without Inside Information, and a Designated Person additionally needs prior written approval from the Company Secretary and General Counsel (or Chairman), valid for 7 business days, with directors confirming the dealing within 2 days. The loan leg secured against already-held vested shares is not caught by the narrower Section 4.5 prohibition, which only bans acquiring securities using margin finance, so pledging existing shares as collateral is permitted subject to the same Open Period and clearance requirements. Overall: the structure is workable only for non-remuneration shares, timed to an Open Period with the required clearance and confirmations, and is unavailable for the more common case of shares originating from an Elders equity incentive or savings scheme.
